Welcome to today's discussion on the history of computing. We will cover some of the
most important milestones that shaped the modern digital world, from early mechanical
calculators to the rise of personal computers and the internet.

In the mid-twentieth century, researchers began building electronic computers that
could perform complex calculations far faster than any human. Early machines like ENIAC
filled entire rooms and required teams of engineers to operate them. Despite their size,
these pioneering systems laid the groundwork for everything that followed.

By the 1970s, advances in semiconductor technology made it possible to fit thousands
of transistors onto a single chip. This breakthrough led directly to the microprocessor,
which in turn made the personal computer a practical reality for ordinary people. The
pace of innovation accelerated rapidly, and within a generation, computing power that
once required a warehouse could fit comfortably in a pocket.
